support_spans: large, solid masses in both testes
pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types: small cells, medium cells, and large cells

concepts.why: The presence of large, solid masses in both testes and a pleomorphic tumor are characteristic of teratoma, but the absence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses is not typical.

The lack of evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on the positron emission tomography–computed tomography scan rules out lymphoma as a primary diagnosis but the test was performed to evaluate for lymphoid malignancy.

rationales.F04: Bilateral testicular enlargement with large solid masses is more typical of germ cell tumors than lymphoma.
rationales.F05: Normal serum tumor markers decrease the likelihood of choriocarcinoma and some other germ cell tumors.
rationales.F06: Absence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses makes lymphoma less likely.
rationales.F07: A large tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion is concerning for aggressive testicular cancer, such as embryonal carcinoma or mixed germ cell tumor.
rationales.F08: A pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types is characteristic of mixed germ cell tumors.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types and the lack of elevated serum tumor markers decided it.
